title: Chronic type II interferon promotes tumor growth through mitochondrial RNA-induced type I interferon and prostaglandin synthesis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both processed count matrices from the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) FTP site: GSE330381 (human A375 melanoma, 27,234 gene rows x 21 sample columns, raw integer counts, library sizes 39-56 million reads) and GSE307168 (mouse YUMM1.7 melanoma, 24,537 gene rows x 24 columns, 18-47 million reads); zero duplicate gene symbols in either. Read both series_matrix metadata files, confirming the full design (control, acute 24 h and chronic 28 d exposure to interferon alpha, beta or gamma, 3 replicates each, one cell line per species). Listed the FTP supplementary directories of all four linked series and read the file list for the chromatin series.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The paper itself is paywalled (Europe PMC: isOpenAccess N; author manuscript PMC13634221 not retrievable as full text), so the biology - double-stranded mitochondrial RNA release, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) synthesis, restored anti-PD1 response - comes from the abstract and GEO series summaries only. I did not open the 2.3 GB CUT&RUN (a method for mapping where a protein binds DNA) tar or the 1.8 GB ATAC-seq (a method for mapping open chromatin) tar; their contents are known only from the GEO file list, which shows bigWig coverage tracks, not peak tables.

a1_downloadable.note: Both RNA-seq count matrices download openly from GEO FTP without login (856 KB and 789 KB gzipped); verified by downloading and parsing them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For a sample-level task the labels (treatment: control/alpha/beta/gamma; time: acute/chronic) are explicit columns in the GEO series_matrix metadata I read. For a gene-level task the label would be a fold change I would have to compute myself.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene-by-sample raw integer counts with gene symbols are present in the files; no accession lookups needed for a sample-level task.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are raw sequencing read counts per gene, stated in the file names (Raw_Counts, RawCounts) and confirmed as integers on inspection; normalization would be mine to choose.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The independent unit is the sample: 21 human + 24 mouse bulk RNA-seq libraries, just 3 replicates per condition, from one cell line per species. That is far under the ~400 rows needed even for a classification task. Counting 27,234 genes as rows is the same trap as the rejected scCT-DB candidate: gene rows are not independent and all derive from 3 replicates per group.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.02 GB for both count matrices; 4.1 GB if the CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq bigWig archives were added
a6_fits_laptop.note: The tabular part is trivially small; the chromatin archives (2.3 GB + 1.8 GB) exceed the 50 MB download rule and were recorded by metadata only.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sample counts in the files match the GEO records exactly (21, 24, 37, 10); the paper's own text was not retrievable to cross-check, so this rests on GEO alone.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are experimenter-assigned treatment conditions, not another model's output, and are not computable from the count features except in the sense the experiment intends.

existing_models.name: Enformer (a deep neural network predicting gene expression from DNA sequence, Avsec et al., Nature Methods 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported strong across-gene correlation on held-out human genomic regions; authors and later reviewers note it predicts differences between genes far better than differences between conditions or individuals.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer to unseen cell types and condition-specific responses; distal enhancer effects beyond ~10 kb.

existing_models.name: Borzoi (a successor model predicting RNA-seq coverage from sequence, Linder et al., Nature Genetics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published as accurate for RNA-seq coverage and variant effects on held-out sequence; not evaluated on chronic-cytokine response in a single cell line.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Adapting to unseen cell types and conditions without retraining.

existing_models.name: Interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) signature classifiers separating type I from type II interferon response (e.g. J Transl Med 2025 network meta-analysis signatures; ISG risk-score classifiers in cancer cohorts)
existing_models.score_and_split: Signature-based scores validated in bulk and single-cell datasets and in The Cancer Genome Atlas cohorts; typically simple gene-set scores rather than released model weights.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Distinguishing acute from chronic interferon states robustly across tissues.

backbone.name: Enformer / Borzoi / AlphaGenome (DNA sequence backbones) for a gene-level reframe; none needed for the sample-level task
backbone.hardware: Running a DNA backbone over ~24,000 promoters is a GPU job; on a 16 GB CPU laptop it would take days
backbone.licence: Enformer and Borzoi weights are open; AlphaGenome weights are non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) melanoma bulk RNA-seq, or the Library of Integrated Network-based Cellular Signatures (LINCS) L1000 perturbation profiles
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the chronic-interferon transcriptional state defined in these two cell lines mark the tumours in patient cohorts that fail anti-PD1 therapy? - a real question, but one answered with a gene signature score, not with a model trained on these 45 samples.

controls.positive_control: Classic interferon-stimulated genes (STAT1, IRF1, CXCL10, GBP2) must rise under all interferon treatments; a pipeline that misses this is broken.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle treatment labels across the 45 samples and confirm any classifier collapses to chance - but with 3 replicates per group this test has almost no power.
controls.external_validation: Public interferon-stimulation RNA-seq in other melanoma lines, or TCGA melanoma ISG scores; the mouse series can also check whether a human-trained signature transfers across species.

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained here could only claim: in one human melanoma line (A375) and one mouse melanoma line (YUMM1.7), with three replicates per condition, these genes separate 28-day from 24-hour interferon exposure - a description of 45 libraries from one laboratory, not a predictive claim about tumours or patients.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a tumour cell's gene activity profile to predict whether it has had brief or long-term interferon exposure.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene-by-sample read-count tables from two melanoma cell lines: 21 human A375 libraries and 24 mouse YUMM1.7 libraries, each a control or a 24-hour or 28-day treatment with interferon alpha, beta or gamma, three replicates per condition (verified by opening the files).
plain_idea.predict: The exposure label (none / acute / chronic, and which interferon), which comes from the experimenters' own treatment schedule recorded in the GEO metadata, not from a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If a chronic-interferon fingerprint could be read off a tumour's transcriptome, oncologists might flag patients whose melanoma will resist anti-PD1 immunotherapy - but with only 45 libraries from two cell lines this dataset can at best suggest the genes, not fit such a model.

more_or_better_data.why: 45 bulk RNA-seq libraries from two cell lines is tiny against the thousands of profiles behind existing interferon-signature work and the genome-wide training sets behind Enformer and Borzoi.

confidence_score.why: Three replicates per condition allow a crude noise estimate but nowhere near enough groups to calibrate per-prediction confidence.

models_beatable.why: Sequence-to-expression models (Enformer 2021, Borzoi 2025) are known to predict condition-specific changes poorly, and a 2025 Nature Methods benchmark found deep perturbation models do not beat linear baselines - but beating them needs far more data than 45 libraries.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data joins to this on a shared key that measures the same quantity the same way; other interferon studies use different cell lines, doses and platforms, so adding them changes the experiment rather than extending it.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a classifier on bulk RNA-seq profiles to call acute versus chronic interferon exposure and the interferon type, then score public melanoma cohorts for a chronic-interferon state. Also considered a gene-level reframe - predict each gene's chronic-interferon fold change from its promoter sequence with a DNA backbone - which fails on effective sample size (3 replicates, one cell line per species), needs a GPU, and lands in the crowded, benchmark-beaten sequence-to-expression field.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the files I actually parsed: two gzipped matrices totalling 1.6 MB, loaded in seconds; any model on 45 samples trains instantly. The GPU estimate applies only to the rejected sequence-backbone reframe over ~24,000 promoters.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the sample columns in the GEO count matrices - 21 and 24, with 3 replicates per condition. That takes one minute and kills the project.

verdict_reason: Part A5 fails decisively: the data is a well-executed mechanistic experiment - 21 human A375 and 24 mouse YUMM1.7 bulk RNA-seq libraries, three replicates per condition, one cell line per species, plus 37 CUT&RUN and 10 ATAC-seq libraries supplied only as multi-gigabyte coverage tracks. Everything downloads cleanly and the labels are honest experimenter-assigned conditions, but 45 independent units is an order of magnitude below the threshold for any supervised model, and treating the 27,234 gene rows as samples would repeat the scCT-DB mistake of counting the wrong unit. The only defensible use is as a gene list or a validation set for work grounded in a larger resource.
